sources.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash model card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The complete September 2 card explicitly names Gemini 3.7 Flash as the base and architecture reference. Its exact-model benchmark and safety tables contain no total or activated-parameter count. Named-base lineage is valid evidence in principle, but no base size is supplied here.

sources.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash API model reference
sources.evidence: Stable model code gemini-3.8-flash; 1,048,576 input tokens; text, image, video, audio and PDF inputs; text output; thinking at low/medium/high levels and function calling supported. Page updated October 22, 2026. Reopened October 27 for the parameter re-audit: the exact stable-model specifications supply no total or active model size.

sources.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber
sources.evidence: September 2, 2026 launch announcement introduces standard Gemini 3.8 Flash separately from the restricted Flash Cyber variant. Fresh October 27 reread found no numerical parameter count; more thinking tokens and benchmark improvements are not model-size disclosures.

sources.title: Gemini 3.7 Flash model card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 review of the complete original PDF. It explicitly identifies Gemini 3.6 Flash as the base and architecture reference, without total or active parameter counts. Comparison tables report capability and safety rather than sizes.

sources.title: Gemini 3.6 Flash model card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 full-card review confirms the explicit Gemini 3.5 Flash base and architecture reference. No numerical total or active count or parameter-bearing structural change is specified.

sources.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash model card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 full-card review confirms the explicit Gemini 3 Flash base and architecture reference. Its benchmark and safety comparisons supply no total or activated-parameter count.

sources.title: Gemini 3 Flash model card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 complete PDF review confirms Gemini 3 Pro as the named base and architecture reference. It publishes no total or active size for Flash or the base.

sources.title: Gemini 3 Pro model card, updated May 2026
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 full review of the May 2026 card: the base is a sparse MoE Transformer that routes tokens to a subset of experts. No numerical total, active count, expert dimensions or routing width is supplied. The card explicitly says Pro is not a modification or fine-tune of a previous model.

sources.title: Developer's guide to Gemini 3.8 Flash
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The current guide compares exact 3.8 and 3.7 Flash benchmark scores and API capabilities, with no total/activated-parameter row. Its parameter references concern sampling, thinking and function-call settings, not learned weights.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon model card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 full-card review for later disclosure. The October 13 Argon card supplies no retrospective Gemini 3.8 Flash total or active count. Argon is explicitly a new model, not a modification or fine-tune of a prior model; no successor count is transferred backward.

sources.title: Gemini API Additional Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Service access is governed by Google API and Gemini additional terms, including restrictions on extracting or replicating model weights; supports proprietary API-access classification.

sources.title: Models.dev Gemini 3.8 Flash record
sources.evidence: Baseline lead records the stable identifier's release date and capabilities. Technical claims were checked against Google's model card and API documentation.

sources.title: Gemini API release notes — September 2, 2026
sources.evidence: The dated September 2 entry explicitly records the GA release of gemini-3.8-flash.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Safety & Security Report
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 search of the complete report text and exact-model comparisons. Gemini 3.8 Flash appears as a comparator and monitor in safety and capability evaluations; none supplies a numerical model size. The three parameter passages concern task difficulty, protection of weights and encoded knowledge, not total or activated counts.

sources.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash Model Evaluation: Approach, Methodology & Results
sources.evidence: Followed the original card link on October 27 to the complete four-page September 2026 evaluation appendix. It explicitly identifies gemini-3.8-flash and describes benchmark methodology, inference settings and results. It provides no total or activated-parameter count. Visually checked the image-based results table on page 4: price and benchmark rows only, with no size column.

name.note: Official name for the stable gemini-3.8-flash API identifier; not Flash Cyber.

developer.note: Google DeepMind model published and served by Google; preserves the catalog's Google developer label.

family.note: Google's developer guide explicitly places this model in the Gemini Flash line; normalized catalog family key.

release_date.note: Dated first-party launch announcement introduces this standard variant on September 2; the model card carries the same date.

open_weights.note: Official distribution is through Google products and APIs under service terms, with no public weight distribution offered.

license.note: Descriptive classification for Google's restricted service access, not an open-weight license or the documentation page's content license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 exact-name/ID total-size and named-base searches, reopened original sources and later primary comparisons found no supported nominal total. The explicit 3.8 Flash to 3.7, 3.6, 3.5, 3 Flash and 3 Pro dependency chain is valid lineage evidence, but none of the named bases has a published count in the reviewed material. Null reflects absent numerical evidence, not an exact tensor-census requirement.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 active/activated-count searches and original/later comparison-table checks found no numerical active count for this model or its named bases. Sparse routing is qualitative, without expert dimensions or routing quantities sufficient for a count. Thinking-token use, benchmark scores, API parameters and successor-model comparisons do not establish a per-token active size.

architecture.note: The 3.8 card explicitly refers architecture to 3.7, then 3.6, then 3.5, then 3 Flash, then 3 Pro. The endpoint card specifies sparse MoE Transformer architecture. This follows the documented architecture references; no sibling size or expert counts are assumed.

context_window.note: Google documents 1,048,576 as the input token limit; maximum output is separately 65,536.

modalities.note: Exact stable-model reference lists these supported data types; PDF is retained as a supported input format.

reasoning.note: Thinking is explicitly supported with low, medium and high levels; minimal is unsupported.

description.value: Google's multimodal reasoning model based on Gemini 3.7 Flash, with text output, configurable thinking levels, and function calling.
description.note: Replaces the promotional intelligence superlative with documented lineage, modalities, thinking controls and function calling.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit: explicit total and active nulls retained after fresh exact-model searches, reopened original card/API/launch and named-base chain, evaluation appendix, current Cloud guide and later Argon card/safety comparisons. The explicit lineage is valid but supplies no count because its bases also lack a numerical disclosure. All unrelated field assessments are preserved.
